The best grid so far is iso_3.15: KL=0.43614 (E514ab09c524e) at 3.14795 bits per weight, against a budget of 3.1484375. That leaves about 0.0005 bits per weight, roughly 0.2M bits, so any upgrade has to be paid for by downgrades.

Where the loss sits: the largest single-layer losses are 3-bit MLP layers.
- 27.up_proj on gptq_int3: 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded). gptq_int4 would give 0.00217 (Efea8c18d2abc).
- 27.gate_proj on rht_gptq_int3: 0.00499 (Efa0bb391da67). rht_gptq_int4 would give 0.00153 (Ef428ac081334).
- 3.up_proj: 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5). gptq_int4 would give 0.00238 (Ef4ee8cb4969e).
- 2.up_proj: 0.00642 (E9baa10763ebe). gptq_int4 would give 0.00237 (Ef3d9c7b4502c).

Bit costs I inferred: from the bits_delta field, int3 costs about 3.15 bits per weight and int2 about 2.14. I assumed int4 costs about 4.15, so an int3-to-int4 upgrade adds about 1 bit per weight.

Why not fund upgrades by dropping MLP layers to int2: for 14.down_proj, rht_gptq_int2 loses 0.00633 versus 0.00181 for rht_gptq_int3. That costs more than an upgrade gains.

Funding plan: use the tabled downgrades, which are predicted to cost only 1e-5 to 4e-5 each. These are the o_proj layers going to 3 bits (2M weights each) and 7.gate_proj going to gptq_int3 (3M weights). I assumed these layers are on 4-bit methods now, so each downgrade saves about 1 bit per weight.

Three proposals, each a superset of the previous one:
- p1: one upgrade.
- p2: two upgrades.
- p3: four upgrades.
